title: "Digital in Air: A GST Tragedy"

# The Inheritance

Ravi took over the family trucking business in the summer of 2021,
twelve trucks and forty employees, along with a GST registration that
had accumulated nearly a crore in unutilized Input Tax Credit. His
father had run the operation for thirty years, filed every return on
time, and died on a ventilator without logging into the GST portal one
last time. A minor oversight, Ravi would learn, with major consequences.

Uncle Sundar, who had retired from a government accounts office, was the
first to offer reassurance. \"Section 18(3),\" he said, tapping his
phone screen with the confidence of a man who read tax journals at
breakfast. \"Rule 41. The law is clear. You are the legal heir. The
credit follows the business. Just file the transfer form and move on.\"

Ravi nodded and opened his laptop. The GST portal loaded in its usual
shade of government blue. He entered his father\'s credentials.

> Your GSTIN is CANCELLED. You cannot perform this action.

He refreshed. He cleared the cache. He called his nephew who \"knew
computers.\" The portal remained unmoved. A dead man\'s login, it
seemed, was not entitled to perform living man\'s transactions.

# The Officer and the Missing Button

GST Bhavan in Delhi is a building designed to make you feel small before
you reach the counter. Ravi arrived with a red folder thick enough to
stop a door: death certificate, legal heirship affidavit, CA-audited
ledgers, three years of returns, and a printout of Circular No.
96/15/2019 that Uncle Sundar had highlighted in yellow.

Mr. Sharma, the jurisdictional officer, read through the file with
genuine sympathy. \"Your case is strong,\" he said. \"Legally, you are
absolutely entitled to this credit.\"

\"So you can approve it, sir?\"

Sharma turned his monitor around. It displayed the same government blue
that Ravi had stared at for weeks. \"Do you see a button here?\"

\"A button?\"

\"For manual transfer. For overriding the system. For acknowledging that
people occasionally die before filing Form ITC-02. There is no button.
The software was built by people who assumed the deceased would politely
log in, initiate the transfer, and only then proceed to the afterlife.
Your father did not follow the correct sequence.\"

\"He was unconscious, sir.\"

\"A common excuse.\"

# The Expensive Certainty

Suresh, the most expensive chartered accountant in East Delhi, took the
case with the enthusiasm of a man who had already priced the litigation.
\"We will file a writ petition,\" he announced, sliding a fee note
across his glass desk. \"The High Court will direct the department to
manually transfer the credit.\"

\"Is there no administrative way? A letter? A request?\"

Suresh laughed. It was a short, expensive laugh. \"The portal is the
administration. The portal has spoken. When software says no, the
officer cannot say yes. This is Digital India. The only human left in
the loop is the judge.\"

Six months later, Ravi stood in the Delhi High Court corridor, holding
paper books bound in blue covers. Inside, the bench heard the matter for
exactly twelve minutes.

\"Why is this man in court for a simple credit transfer?\" the judge
asked the government counsel.

\"The portal has no provision for post-cancellation transfer, Your
Honour.\"

\"Then ask GSTN to create one.\"

\"We have, Your Honour.\"

\"And?\"

\"They said they will consider it in the next update.\"

\"When is that?\"

The counsel looked at his shoes. \"There is no date, Your Honour.\"

The judge sighed and dictated an order directing the department to
manually adjust the credit, noting that \"substantive rights cannot be
held hostage to software limitations.\"

# The Victory

The credit was transferred. The business survived. Ravi paid the lawyer,
paid the CA, and paid in sleepless nights for a right that the statute
had already given him for free.

He never did find out which update GSTN was waiting for. The portal,
last he checked, still displayed the same message to anyone who tried to
file ITC-02 from a cancelled registration. Silent. Unfeeling. Utterly
dominant.

# Technical Analysis

****Statutory Basis****

-   Section 18(3) of the CGST Act, 2017: Transfer of unutilized ITC in
    cases of death, succession, or business transfer.
-   Rule 41(1) of the CGST Rules, 2017: Prescribes Form GST ITC-02 as
    the mechanism.
-   Circular No. 96/15/2019-GST (\[CBIC\](<https://cbic-gst.gov.in>)):
    Confirms the procedure but assumes an active transferor GSTIN.

****The Deadlock****

The portal enforces a hard validation: ITC-02 submission requires the
transferor GSTIN to be in \"Active\" status. In practice, the sequence
is:

1.  Proprietor dies.
2.  Registration is cancelled (Form REG-16, reason: death).
3.  Heir obtains new GSTIN.
4.  Heir attempts ITC-02 → rejected because transferor GSTIN is
    cancelled.

There is no backend override, no offline SOP, and no exception flag for
deceased transferors.

****Judicial Remedy****

Multiple High Courts (Delhi, Madras, Gujarat) have held that substantive
statutory rights cannot be defeated by software constraints. Remedy:
Writ petition under Article 226 of the Constitution, seeking a mandamus
to the department to manually adjust the ITC ledger.

****Systemic Gap****

  Issue                                       Status
  ------------------------------------------- -------------------
  Portal patch for post-cancellation ITC-02   Not implemented
  Manual SOP for jurisdictional officers      Not notified
  Alternative form (e.g., ITC-02A)            Does not exist
  GSTN timeline for fix                       No published date

****References****

1.  CGST Act, 2017 --- Section 18(3):
    <https://www.cbic.gov.in/htdocs-cbec/gst/cgst-act>
2.  CGST Rules, 2017 --- Rule 41:
    <https://www.cbic.gov.in/htdocs-cbec/gst/cgst-rules>
3.  Circular No. 96/15/2019-GST: <https://cbic-gst.gov.in>
4.  Constitution of India --- Article 226 (Writ jurisdiction)

****Summary****

The law grants the right. The portal denies the mechanism. The only
remaining interface is a High Court bench. Digital India, in this case,
is less a platform and more a toll gate.
